assessment.rationale: No open or discoverable solution makes staple crops drought-proof, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 people growing drought-proof crops is far from met. The best deployed answers are drought-tolerant, not drought-proof. HB4 wheat, approved in Argentina, gave a 13 percent field yield advantage under reproductive-stage water deficit in INTA's April 2026 Field Crops Research study and had about 100,000 ha planted cumulatively by 2024 (https://repositorio.inta.gob.ar/handle/20.500.12123/25002). DTMA drought-tolerant maize out-yields checks in managed trials, but in Malawi's 2011/12 early-season drought it did no better than other improved maize (https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s12571-015-0511-4), and modelled gains are 3 to 20 percent. Cereal losses in drought years still average 13.7 percent globally, and the UNCCD frames even 25 to 30 percent drought yield gains as tolerance, not immunity (https://www.unccd.int/resources/unccd-library/new-hostile-climate-drought-tolerant-crops-systems-needed-unprecedented). Europe PMC returns only 6 records for the phrase drought-proof crop, none reporting such a crop. Honest limit: drought tolerance in maize, wheat and sorghum is a mature field with released varieties, so tasks that re-breed or re-test HB4 or DTMA-type tolerance are known answers; the open work is crops that hold yield under severe, early or multi-season drought, and each task needs its own basis.

additionalSearches.query: HB4 drought tolerant wheat adoption hectares 2026 yield under drought
additionalSearches.finding: INTA (Field Crops Research, April 2026): HaHB4 wheat yield advantage under reproductive-phase water deficit was 15 percent in the greenhouse and 13 percent in the field. Bioceres reported more than 55,000 ha in 2022-23 and over 100,000 ha cumulative in Argentina; company claims of 20 to 42 percent are less independent. Tolerance, not drought-proofing.

additionalSearches.query: drought tolerant maize Africa adoption DTMA yield advantage severe drought limits
additionalSearches.finding: DTMA varieties out-yielded checks by 83 to 137 percent under managed drought on-farm, but modelled gains are 3 to 20 percent, and in Malawi 2011/12 DT maize did not perform significantly better than other improved maize because the drought struck early. Adoption is limited by seed availability and price.

Europe PMC returns only 6 records for "drought-proof" crop; none reports a drought-proof staple crop (top hits are a 2018 review on improving drought tolerance and sugarcane genotype-by-environment work). Null result for an existing solution.

additionalSearches.query: no crop variety fully drought proof yield losses under severe drought staple crops 2025 2026 study climate
additionalSearches.finding: Cereal production losses averaged 13.7 percent in drought years since 1985 (Nature 2016); over 160 drought-tolerant maize varieties for sub-Saharan Africa yield 25 to 30 percent more under drought, which reduces losses but does not prevent them. No source shows a fully drought-proof variety.
